chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asammi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Fear the easy climb when its descent is steep/difficult.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not leave the soul and its desires unguarded; for its desires are its ruin. Leaving the soul to what it desires is its affliction, and restraining the soul from what it desires is its cure.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of fearing the easy climb with a steep descent in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, presents a dual perspective on self-discipline: Imam al-Rida warns against the deceptive ease of initial spiritual or worldly ascent that leads to a perilous fall, while Imam al-Sadiq emphasizes the intrinsic danger of indulging the *nafs* (soul). Scholarly tradition interprets the 'easy climb' as a metaphor for acquiring status or knowledge without rigorous self-accounting, and the 'ruin' as the inevitable consequence of unchecked desires. The text underscores the Shia ethical principle that true salvation lies in actively curbing the self's whims rather than merely avoiding sin.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asammi, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Fear the easy climb up when there was a bumpy slope down’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was saying: ‘Do not leave the soul and its desires unguarded; its desires are to destroy it. Leaving the soul with its desires unguarded is hurting the soul, however, guarding the soul against its desires is medicine for its illness’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:
“Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) once said to me, ‘Beware of an easy climb up that has a very deep and steep climb down.’

“The narrator has said that Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) would say, ‘Do not leave the soul with its desires unguarded; its desires are to destroy it. Leaving the soul with its desires unguarded is hurting the soul, however, guarding the soul against its desires is medicine for its illness.’”
